key_highlights: ASX closed a volatile week with modest gains as oil prices and bond yields eased; big four banks (CBA, ANZ, NAB, WBC) advanced on rate-hike expectations
RBA issued a blunt hawkish warning days before its next rate decision; IMF separately urged fiscal spending cuts, reinforcing a higher-for-longer rate path
Recession odds for 2027 rose materially, with macrobusiness flagging 'four horsemen' global macro risks (debt, trade, energy, demographics)
Iron ore prices under pressure ('roaches seethe'); LNG flows to Japan outpaced East Coast domestic supply, creating a structural gas shortfall
Gold exploration news positive: Forrestania (four WA prefeasibility studies) and Aurum (high-grade gold, Côte d'Ivoire) support junior miners
Qantas ground staff strike looms over 'Joyce-era' bargaining; Coles (COL.AX) criticised for keeping milk prices elevated post-farmer support axing
Anthropic secured a $31bn datacentre deal in western Queensland, signalling major tech-infrastructure capex into Australia
Housing affordability hit record lows; ACCC moved to break real estate agent monopoly; tenants saw modest rent relief

sectors.trend: Iron ore under pressure; gold exploration positive (Forrestania, Aurum); WA copper-nickel-PGE targets (Dalaroo) add optionality
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face headwinds from soft iron ore; gold juniors (FOR.AX, AUR.AX) and copper names (NEM.AX, STO.AX) offer relative strength

sectors.trend: Big four advanced on hawkish RBA signal and rising rate expectations; state borrowing costs soaring
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX benefit from NIM expansion but face credit-risk concerns if 2027 recession materialises

sectors.trend: Oil prices eased, supporting consumer sentiment; LNG export surge to Japan starves East Coast; Victoria retreated from renewable transmission; coal policy debate intensifies
sectors.implications: WDS.AX, WEL.AX face domestic gas supply constraints; renewable names (SOL.AX, LEM.AX) hit by Victoria policy reversal; coal (BRL.AX, WDS.AX) sees political tailwind

sectors.trend: Petrol price shock pressures household budgets; Coles criticised on milk pricing; Qantas strike risk disrupts travel
sectors.implications: WES.AX, COL.AX face margin pressure; QAN.AX exposed to industrial action; defensive staples preferred in rate-hike environment

sectors.trend: Housing 'absurdly unaffordable'; ACCC targeting agent monopoly; tenants saw modest rent relief
sectors.implications: REITs (GPW.AX, ICPS.AX) benefit from rent relief but face affordability-driven demand risk; ACCC action could compress agent margins

sectors.trend: Anthropic $31bn QLD datacentre deal signals major tech capex; ASX small-cap runners (Latrobe, CurveBeam, Arrow, Sultan) show breadth
sectors.implications: Datacentre/infrastructure plays (SGH.AX, VMC.AX) gain; small-cap momentum supports speculative flows

key_themes: Hawkish RBA + IMF fiscal tightening = higher-for-longer rates, pressuring growth and property
Commodity divergence: iron ore weak, gold strong, LNG supply imbalance
2027 recession probability rising, shifting market toward defensives
Energy policy fragmentation across states (Victoria renewables retreat, coal debate)
Tech infrastructure super-cycle entering Australia via datacentre capex
Industrial risk: Qantas strike, Coles pricing controversy

risk_assessment.mitigation: Overweight short-duration bonds; favour banks with strong NIM; underweight rate-sensitive REITs and growth equities
Maintain 15-20% cash allocation; favour dividend-paying defensives (WES.AX, CSL.AX); hedge with gold (GOLD.AX)
Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX exposure; rotate into gold and copper miners
Avoid QAN.AX ahead of strike; monitor Qantas-linked tourism and retail names

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Middle East oil shock / energy supply
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hold energy hedges; monitor WDS.AX, WEL.AX for LNG supply disruption
Underweight property-linked REITs; monitor bank NPL trends; favour unlisted or fixed-income alternatives

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold miners and exploration names
opportunities.rationale: Forrestania and Aurum discoveries plus safe-haven flows from recession fears support gold equities

opportunities.recommendation: Add to big four banks on rate-hike tailwind
opportunities.rationale: RBA hawkishness and IMF fiscal tightening support NIM expansion; banks advanced on the week
Anthropic $31bn QLD deal signals multi-year capex cycle benefiting infrastructure and power names
Petrol shock and recession risk shift demand to essentials; WES and CSL offer dividend resilience

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore / thermal coal exposure
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore under pressure; China demand uncertain; coal policy risk in Victoria

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge rate risk with short-duration bonds and cash
defensive_moves.rationage: RBA hike imminent; state borrowing costs soaring; 2027 recession odds rising

defensive_moves.rationale: Qantas strike risk; housing affordability at extremes; ACCC regulatory overhang on property

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain range-bound to slightly lower into the RBA decision. Hawkish RBA + IMF fiscal warning cap upside; bank strength and oil easing provide a floor. Volatility elevated. Qantas strike and petrol shock add consumer-side pressure. Expect ^AXJO to trade in a tight band with sector rotation toward defensives.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautious. Rising 2027 recession probability, housing affordability crisis, and state debt burden weigh on growth. However, gold/copper exploration pipeline, tech datacentre capex, and bank NIM expansion offer structural pockets of strength. A soft-landing scenario remains possible if commodity prices stabilise and RBA pivots by mid-2027.
